links.note: Narrate your own experience of being out alone in a thunderstorm - the counterpart of the pilot meeting the huge storm cloud.
The compass was not working and the radio was dead - the pilot's instruments failing inside the cloud.
The mood at the start of 'Black Aeroplane' - happy and excited, stars shining, hoping to reach England in his old Dakota. The opening of the journey.
Evaluating the narrator's decision not to turn back to Paris - the choice that took him into the storm.
How the narrator found himself lost after Paris Control could no longer hear him - the journey inside the cloud.
What happened when he turned twelve degrees west towards England - a step of the flight into the storm.
Why the writer felt frightened once again - the fuel and the dark cloud on his journey.
The values that helped him endure the critical situation - drawn from the whole flight into the storm with no fuel to spare.
Why he could see nothing outside the aeroplane - he was inside the black cloud.
How to describe the 'risk' the narrator took - flying into a storm cloud in an old Dakota with little fuel.
The purpose of calling Paris Control - part of the pilot's journey before the storm.
What sort of aeroplane he saw in the black clouds - a black aeroplane with no lights. That is the mysterious guide of 24159.
How the narrator came out of the clouds and reached safely - following the guide down to the runway. 24160 is that landing.
Why he says he was not sorry to walk away from the old Dakota - his relief on the ground after landing safely.
What he saw when he looked down - the lights of a big city, once he was out of the cloud and coming in to land.
The points that went on troubling Forsyth's mind after landing safely - the identity of the other pilot, which the story never explains.
What made the woman in the control centre look at him strangely - there had been no other aeroplane. The unexplained ending.
The woman at the control tower confirmed there was no other aeroplane - the fact that leaves the ending unresolved.
Who you think helped the narrator, with reasons - the question invites the reader's own reading, hallucination or guardian, which is 24162.
Who narrates 'Black Aeroplane' - Frederick Forsyth. 24151 names him as the author of the pilot's story.
